investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. The 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining VM slots (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. Because the pod never scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885) never completed, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the contract validation to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.title: image-generation-stream Eval Failure: OpenAI API Credit Balance Exhausted on /api/generate/image/stream
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API key used by the eval runner has exhausted its credit balance, causing the upstream image generation call to return a hard error (code: credit_balance_exhausted). The stream terminated with a generation_error frame instead of the required generation_completed frame, so both contract assertions — frameTypes containing "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent equaling true — were violated.
investigation.rootCause: The OpenAI organization account associated with the API key used by the eval runner at /api/generate/image/stream has zero remaining credits. The upstream API rejected the image generation request with type "insufficient_quota" and code "credit_balance_exhausted", causing the AURA backend to emit a generation_error SSE frame and terminate the stream without producing a completion artifact. This is an external billing/quota condition, not a code defect in the eval runner or the image generation route itself. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; this is an eval infrastructure failure scoped to the observability probe environment.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. The 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining VM slots (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. Because the pod never scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885) never completed, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the contract validation to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource pool on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero allocatable VM slots for new pods at the time of the eval run.

[Likely contributing] The node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes; if those nodes are saturated there is no fallback, making the cluster effectively at zero schedulable capacity for this workload.

[Possible] A recent scale-down, node failure, or maintenance event reduced the number of kata-capable nodes from a higher baseline to 2, shrinking the available VM slot pool without a corresponding reduction in demand.

[Possible] The eval probe itself, or a prior cleanup that did not complete, left one or more remote-agent VMs running and consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, reducing headroom for the next probe run.

[Lower confidence] A misconfiguration in the pod's resource request for kata.peerpods.io/vm (e.g., requesting more slots than any single node can provide) could cause permanent Unschedulable status even on an otherwise healthy cluster; however, the fact that 2 nodes are listed as candidates (not affinity-mismatched) suggests the request quantity is plausible but the pool is simply exhausted.
